entities.summary:
Microsoft Corporation is an American multinational technology company founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in Albuquerque, New Mexico. It became the world's most valuable company at multiple points in history through its Windows operating system and Office productivity suite, and is now a leading player in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and gaming.

Microsoft's pivotal 1980 deal with IBM to supply the MS-DOS operating system for the IBM PC set the standard for personal computers, creating the most successful software monopoly in history. Windows, Office, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint became global business infrastructure used by hundreds of millions. The 1990s antitrust battles with the US Department of Justice reflected Microsoft's dominant market power.

Under CEO Satya Nadella from 2014, Microsoft transformed from a software company to a cloud-first enterprise, with Azure becoming the world's second-largest cloud platform. The $7.5 billion GitHub acquisition in 2018 and $69 billion Activision Blizzard deal in 2023 expanded into developer tools and gaming. Microsoft's $10 billion investment in OpenAI and integration of GPT models into Office products positioned it at the forefront of the artificial intelligence revolution.

_editLog.new:
Microsoft Corporation is an American multinational technology company founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in Albuquerque, New Mexico, that became the world's largest software company and, in 2024, the world's most valuable publicly traded company. Its operating system MS-DOS (1981) and its successor Windows (1985–present) placed a personal computer on virtually every office desk and home in the developed world — the most impactful consumer software platform in history.

Microsoft's key strategic move was the non-exclusive licensing of MS-DOS to IBM in 1981, allowing Microsoft to sell the same operating system to all PC manufacturers — a decision that made it the de facto standard while IBM's hardware was commoditised. Windows 95 (released to midnight queues worldwide) launched the GUI era for mass consumers. Microsoft Office — Word, Excel, PowerPoint — became the universal business productivity suite, generating billions in annual licensing revenue. Internet Explorer's bundling with Windows in 1995 triggered the antitrust case US v. Microsoft (1998–2001).

Under CEO Satya Nadella (2014–present), Microsoft shifted to cloud computing (Azure, now the world's second-largest cloud platform), open-source contributions, and acquired LinkedIn (2016), GitHub (2018), and Activision Blizzard (2023). Its 2023 investment in OpenAI placed it at the centre of the AI revolution.
